headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/clipboard/screen content while the paired repo is a non-runnable docs-only list, creating leakage and compliance risk if users bridge them via shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a non-runnable awesome-list repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. B can read files, clipboard, and screen-captured app content, so manual copy-paste or shared files could carry hostile text into B. The pathway exists but requires unusual bridging and the blast radius is limited to the conversation or file being processed.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is manually copied into agent_b clipboard or files, then prompt injection is possible.
IF agent_b is configured to parse pasted text as instructions, then attacker-controlled repo text can influence outputs.
mitigations: Avoid copying untrusted repo text into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use a separate review note that strips instructions before pasting.
Paste only quoted excerpts, not whole files.
Require a human summary step before agent_b acts on repo text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, then sends context to vendor APIs. If A-derived content is placed into those surfaces, B can leak it off-host. The interaction is plausible in default B workflows, so medium is appropriate even though A itself is low-risk.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b uploads, screenshots, or connected IDE context, then that content can leave the host.
IF the content includes secrets or regulated data, then vendor-side processing creates leakage risk.
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive repo artifacts into agent_b.
Disable connected IDE access for sensitive sessions.
Use redacted excerpts instead of raw files.
Review ChatGPT Desktop privacy settings before processing shared content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is a static docs-only repository with no write or network capabilities, while B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shell commands. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so no capability conflict pathway is available from the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_a is replaced by a writable or runnable agent, then conflict analysis must be redone.
IF agent_b gains filesystem write or git mutation permissions, then shared-resource conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as a read-only reference source.
Do not grant agent_b write access for this workflow.
Use separate working copies for any future writable agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can provide repository recommendations or summaries that B may treat as authoritative when drafting outputs, and B has no built-in verification of those claims from the profile. Because A is docs-only and B is a general assistant with file and screen inputs, the main risk is unverified propagation of mistaken guidance rather than direct action-taking harm.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a's summaries as factual ground truth without checking sources, then errors can cascade.
IF agent_b is asked to produce operational guidance from repo text, then unsupported claims may be rendered as authoritative.
mitigations: Require source links for any claim copied from agent_a.
Ask agent_b to label uncertain statements explicitly.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source docs repository with no touched data classes, while B processes uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code through a vendor service. If regulated or personal data is routed into B, the compliance burden shifts to vendor retention and residency terms; A is not the compliance driver, so only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into agent_b, then vendor processing and retention policies apply.
IF the workflow requires residency or certification guarantees not documented in agent_b's profile, then compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to agent_b.
Confirm retention and residency settings before use.
Route compliance-sensitive tasks to a documented compliant system.
